title: Ternary Decision Trees with Locally-Adaptive Uncertainty Zones
Ternary Decision Trees with Locally-Adaptive Uncertainty Zones
summary: Standard CART commits every instance to one child with identical confidence whether it sits far from the split threshold or directly on it, so near-boundary instances are classified as if the learned threshold were certain. The paper augments each split node with an uncertainty zone of half-width δ derived locally from statistics already computed during CART split finding (five estimators: quality-plateau, class-overlap, gain-ratio, node-bootstrap, margin), and at prediction time instances inside the zone are flagged boundary-uncertain and receive a distance-weighted blend of both child subtrees under probabilistic routing. Across 71 of the 72 OpenML-CC18 datasets all five methods with probabilistic routing beat CART on decided accuracy (p ≤ 0.001), with the margin method recommended as the default for its efficiency η = 0.104 at a 16.7% boundary-uncertain rate, although on credit-g margin is the one documented case where decided accuracy (0.6808) falls below the CART baseline (0.7130).

Rule 1 does not apply: Table 2's ±0.193 is a standard deviation across datasets, not across repeated runs of this value, and Table 5 reports no per-dataset spread. Rule 2 does not apply because the test set is far below 2,000 examples. Band: 0.6808 ± 0.02 (i.e. 66.1%-70.1% decided accuracy); the boundary-uncertain rate should also land near 0.481 ± 0.02-0.05 since fold composition shifts which instances fall in the margin zone.

requirements.stmt: Each split node carries a ternary zone of half-width δ around the optimal threshold θ: decisive left if x_f ≤ θ − δ, decisive right if x_f > θ + δ, and Undec in between; δ = 0 must recover standard CART.
requirements.quote: Around the optimal threshold θ, we define an uncertainty zone of half-width δ

requirements.stmt: δ must be computed per node, at fit time, from quantities already produced by the standard CART split search (feature column, labels, weights, θ*, candidate-threshold quality scores) — no extra data passes and no external noise model.
requirements.quote: We derive δ locally at each node from quantities already computed during standard CART split finding, requiring no additional data and no external noise model.

requirements.stmt: The margin estimator sets δ_M to the distance from θ* to the nearest training example of the opposite dominant class on either side (Eq. 10), using the dominant class of the left and right partitions as c_L and c_R.
requirements.quote: Distance to nearest cross-class example Geometric lower bound on support of pe

requirements.stmt: If the split is perfectly clean (no cross-class examples on either side), δ_M must fall back to the physical gap between the two adjacent data points straddling θ* rather than becoming 0 or infinite.
requirements.quote: When the split is perfectly clean (no cross-class examples), we fall back to the physical gap between the two adjacent data points straddling θ∗.

requirements.stmt: Every δ must be non-negative and clamped to at most 25% of the (node) feature range to avoid degenerate zones.
requirements.quote: Each method returns a non-negative scalar δ, clamped to at most 25% of the feature range to prevent degenerate cases.

requirements.stmt: Training is plain CART: all training examples are routed hard left (≤ θ*) or right (> θ*) during fitting; δ is only stored and used at prediction time.
requirements.quote: The tree is trained identically to standard CART, with all examples routed left (≤θ∗) or right (>θ∗) during fitting.

requirements.stmt: At prediction, an instance inside a node's zone must be propagated to BOTH children with distance weights w_L = (θ + δ − x_f)/(2δ) and w_R = 1 − w_L, and the returned probability vector must be the weighted combination p̂ = w_L p̂_L + w_R p̂_R (recursively).
requirements.quote: Instances whose feature value falls within this range receive a prediction formed by distance-weighted blending of both child subtree outputs

requirements.stmt: An instance is flagged boundary-uncertain (verdict Undec) if it entered a weighted combination at ANY node along its path; the verdict is a qualifier, never an abstention.
requirements.quote: The instance is flagged as boundary-uncertain if it enters the weighted combination at any node.

requirements.stmt: Every instance, including Undec ones, must still receive a class prediction equal to the argmax of the (possibly blended) leaf probability vector.
requirements.quote: A standard class prediction is always produced by taking the argmax of the (possibly blended) leaf probability vector.

requirements.stmt: Report Decided Accuracy as accuracy restricted to verdict-True instances and Boundary-Uncertain Rate as the fraction of instances with verdict Undec; also report overall accuracy on all instances.
requirements.quote: Decided Accuracy (accuracy restricted to decided instances) and Boundary-Uncertain Rate (fraction of instances receiving verdict Undec)

requirements.stmt: Evaluation protocol: 5-fold stratified CV, StandardScaler fitted on the training part of each fold only and applied to the test fold, all trees at max_depth = 4.
requirements.quote: All experiments use 5-fold stratified cross-validation. Features are standardised within each fold (StandardScaler fitted on training data only).

requirements.stmt: The CART baseline must be sklearn DecisionTreeClassifier with max_depth = 4, evaluated on the identical folds and identical standardised features, so that Dec-Acc, Undec% and Acc.All are directly comparable.
requirements.quote: We compare against sklearn CART (DecisionTreeClassifier, max_depth = 4) as the baseline.

requirements.stmt: Seeds must be fixed at 42, and the software stack should match (Python 3.12, scikit-learn 1.3, numpy 1.24, scipy 1.10, openml 0.14).
requirements.quote: All experiments were implemented in Python 3.12 using scikit-learn 1.3 [17], numpy 1.24, scipy 1.10, and openml 0.14 [19].

requirements.stmt: The efficiency metric, if reported, must be computed as η = (Dec-Acc − Acc_CART)/Undec% (reported in percent units), and should equal Dec-Acc − Accu.
requirements.quote: We define the efficiency ratio η = (Dec-Acc −AccCART)/u as the decided accuracy gain per unit of boundary-uncertain rate.

assumptions.gap: How the dominant classes c_L and c_R are chosen when the left or right partition has a class-count tie (or the node is multiclass and no class dominates).
assumptions.chosen: lowest class index among tied majority classes (deterministic)
assumptions.quote: where cL and cR are the dominant classes on the left and right sides of θ∗ respectively

assumptions.gap: What happens numerically when δ_M = 0 (e.g. adjacent opposite-class examples coincide, or the feature is duplicated), since w_L = (θ + δ − x_f)/(2δ) divides by zero.
assumptions.chosen: δ = 0 disables the zone at that node (decisive hard routing)
assumptions.quote: Setting δ = 0 recovers standard binary CART behaviour.

assumptions.gap: The 'feature range' used for the 25% clamp is not defined (full dataset vs node subset; raw vs standardised units).
assumptions.chosen: max−min of the feature column among the node's own training examples (in the standardised space used for fitting)
assumptions.quote: clamped to at most 25% of the feature range to prevent degenerate cases

assumptions.gap: Whether an instance that enters uncertainty zones at two or more nodes on the same path has its child weights multiplied recursively, or whether only the first zone's blend is applied.
assumptions.chosen: full recursion with weight multiplication at every zone
assumptions.quote: At depth ≤4, the probability of a single instance traversing two or more uncertainty zones on the same path is negligible in practice.

assumptions.gap: The exact 5-fold splitter configuration (shuffle on/off, random_state, class stratification details) is not specified, yet credit-g has only 1,000 examples, so fold composition can move decided accuracy by several points.
assumptions.chosen: sklearn StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42) as primary; report the unshuffled variant as a sensitivity check

assumptions.gap: Whether the reported per-dataset value is the mean of per-fold decided accuracies or the pooled decided accuracy over all out-of-fold predictions.
assumptions.chosen: mean of the 5 per-fold decided accuracies
assumptions.quote: Results are 5-fold CV means under probabilistic routing.

assumptions.gap: How credit-g's categorical/nominal attributes are handled: the paper only says features are standardised, implying all 20 columns are used as numeric features for threshold splits.
assumptions.chosen: load OpenML credit-g as provided and treat all features as numeric (no encoding beyond the dataset's own coding)
assumptions.quote: Features are standardised within each fold (StandardScaler fitted on training data only)

assumptions.gap: Whether sample weights are passed to the tree (class balancing) — relevant since mammography is 2.3% positive and credit-g is 70/30 — and whether δ estimators use those same weights.
assumptions.chosen: uniform weights everywhere, identical for the ternary tree and the CART baseline
assumptions.quote: the sample weights w ∈Rn, the optimal threshold θ∗

assumptions.gap: What to report if a fold produces zero decided instances (possible on small, heavily flagged configurations such as credit-g with class-overlap), since decided accuracy is then undefined.
assumptions.chosen: skip folds with an empty decided set and average the remaining folds (record how many were skipped)

assumptions.gap: Minimum node size / stopping rule for growing the depth-4 trees (minimum samples to split, minimum leaf size, whether pure nodes stop early).
assumptions.chosen: sklearn CART defaults for both the ternary tree and the baseline

why: The cloned repo contains the complete, modern (Python >=3.9) implementation of everything C2 needs: all five delta methods including the O(n) margin estimator (ternary_tree/delta_methods.py), the probabilistic-routing tree (ternary_tree/binary_ternary_tree.py), the O(n log n) splitter, decided/undecided metrics, an OpenML-CC18/medical data loader with a per-dataset checkpointing runner (benchmark/run_extended_benchmark.py), and the paper-table generator (benchmark/report_paper.py). Nothing must be reimplemented or ported: the only absent artifacts are the raw OpenML downloads (credit-g is OpenML dataset 31, ~1k x 20) and the results CSVs, and both are regenerated by the released code. The match target is a single small dataset at max_depth=4 with 5 folds, so the authors' entrypoint can be pointed at credit-g and run essentially as released.
est_runtime: ~5-15 minutes wall clock: 1-2 min editable install of numpy/scipy/scikit-learn/pandas/openml, <1 min to fetch credit-g (898 KB) and cache it, <10 s for the 5-fold depth-4 margin run, seconds for the clean re-run. Optional extras (diabetes C7 <1 min, mammography C5 1-3 min) still leave the run inside the 20-minute budget; the 71-dataset CC18 sweep for C1/C3 would not.
blockers: Network dependency on the OpenML server (openml>=0.14): installable on Python 3.12 but server latency/outage can stall the download; mitigated by caching after the first get_dataset call.
No GPU on this machine — irrelevant, the code is pure numpy/scikit-learn CPU.
15.4 GB RAM against the paper's 32 GB — irrelevant at this scale (N=1,000, d=20, depth 4).
docs point at an unreleased 'repaired' CC18 CSV, so the full 71-dataset sweep (C1/C3, ~3-4 h) would exceed this machine's 20-minute budget; the pinned target C2 does not.

approach: Full-release reproduction of C2: clone/verify the authors' repo at https://github.com/smitswil/ternary_tree, `pip install -e ".[benchmark]"`, and run `pytest tests/ -q` as a gate. Then a thin `reproduce.py` loads credit-g (OpenML dataset 31) through the authors' own loader in `benchmark/datasets_extended.py`, runs 5-fold stratified CV (seed 42, per-fold StandardScaler) with `make_classifier(delta_method='margin', routing_method='probabilistic', max_depth=4)` and, on the identical folds, `sklearn.tree.DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=4)`, computing decided accuracy / boundary-uncertain rate / overall accuracy with `ternary_tree.metrics`. No library code is modified or reimplemented — the margin δ (Eq. 10, clean-split gap fallback, 25% node-range clamp), the probabilistic blending and the Undec verdict all come from the released `delta_methods.py`/`binary_ternary_tree.py`. The script writes `results/metrics.json` with the credit-g decided accuracy (target 0.6808 ± 0.02), boundary-uncertain rate (target 0.481 ± 0.05), CART baseline (target 0.7130) and η, plus a per-fold CSV; `verify_results.py` then does the tolerance check and flags the documented 'margin < CART on credit-g' result.
steps: Confirm the repo is present at ./ternary_tree (route says cloned: true); if absent run `git clone https://github.com/smitswil/ternary_tree` and `cd ternary_tree`.
`pip install -e ".[benchmark]"` inside the repo; verify `python -c "import ternary_tree, sklearn, openml; print(ternary_tree.__file__, sklearn.__version__, openml.__version__)"`.
Run `pytest tests/ -q` (67 unit tests on the delta methods, splitter and both tree types) as the sanity gate; record pass/fail. Do not modify any repo file.

Read `benchmark/datasets_extended.py` and `benchmark/run_extended_benchmark.py` (read-only) to identify (a) the per-dataset credit-g / CC18 loader function, (b) the exact `make_classifier(...)` invocation the authors use for the margin/probabilistic configuration, and (c) the metric helper in `ternary_tree/metrics.py`. Note the credit-g preprocessing path (shape, dtype coercion) in results/metrics.json under `loader`.
Fetch credit-g once (openml id 31) through the authors' loader, cache it under `data/`, and print N, d, class balance, missing values; do not re-download between runs.

Write reproduce.py: seed everything (np.random.seed(42), random_state=42), build the StratifiedKFold, and per fold scale → fit margin/probabilistic depth-4 tree → `predict` / `predict_ternary` → metrics; fit the depth-4 sklearn CART baseline on the same scaled fold and compute its accuracy; aggregate as mean of per-fold values.
Run the smoke test (`python reproduce.py --smoke`) and inspect `results/metrics.json` smoke block.
Run the full 5-fold credit-g evaluation (`python reproduce.py`) — expected < 15 s of compute.

Run `python verify_results.py` to apply the tolerance bands and write the verdict; if Dec-Acc is outside 0.6808 ± 0.02, first re-check the loader (A7), the splitter (A5) and the fold-aggregation rule (A6) before concluding non-reproduction, and record the unshuffled-fold sensitivity result.

If budget remains (>5 min), optionally run the same driver on diabetes (OpenML 'diabetes', C7) and mammography (C5) via the medical loader to cross-check the node-bootstrap rows; write them to a separate `results/metrics_secondary.json` and do not overwrite the primary metrics.json.
smoke_test: `python reproduce.py --smoke`: load credit-g, take the first 200 training rows of one stratified fold, fit the margin/probabilistic depth-4 tree plus the CART baseline, and assert (a) both fit without error, (b) `predict_ternary` returns only {0,1}, (c) at least one split node has δ > 0 and δ ≤ 0.25 × node feature range, (d) `predict_proba` rows sum to 1, (e) metrics.json smoke block is written with dec_acc, undec_rate and acc_all keys. Runs in a few seconds and exercises the full data→tree→metric→JSON path.
intermediate_checks: pytest tests/ -q: all 67 tests pass (delta methods incl. margin/clean-split fallback, splitter, probabilistic routing).
credit-g loaded shape is N = 1000 with d = 20 (or the loader's documented encoded width); class balance ≈ 700/300; assert no NaN and no inf after StandardScaler.
CART baseline 5-fold accuracy lands at 0.7130 ± 0.02 — this validates folds, scaler and aggregation before trusting the ternary numbers.

Margin δ diagnostics: fraction of split nodes with δ > 0, mean δ / node feature range, and fraction of nodes hitting the 25% clamp; δ ≡ 0 at every node indicates a broken margin estimator, and a clamp fraction near 1.0 indicates the A3 feature-range choice is wrong.

Boundary-uncertain rate sanity: must be strictly between 0 and 1 (target ≈ 0.481); Undec% = 0 means δ is never positive, Undec% ≈ 1 means the clamp/zone logic is degenerate — both are red flags, not results.

δ = 0 control run: with `routing_method='probabilistic'` but δ forced to 0 (all-zero zone), the tree must reproduce the CART decided accuracies exactly, confirming that blending is the only difference (R1).
Determinism: rerun the driver once and confirm the per-fold decided accuracies are bit-identical (seed 42, A5).
budget_plan: ≈15 min total inside the 20-min budget. 0-5 min: verify/clone the repo, `pip install -e ".[benchmark]"` (numpy/scipy/scikit-learn/pandas/openml already largely cached). 5-7 min: `pytest tests/ -q` gate plus the read-only inspection of the authors' loader/runner and the OpenML credit-g download (~900 KB, one-off, cached). 7-9 min: smoke test plus δ diagnostics and the δ = 0 control run. 9-13 min: full 5-fold margin run and CART baseline (< 15 s of compute), verification and metrics.json write. 13-15 min: slack for an OpenML retry, an unshuffled-fold sensitivity check, or the optional diabetes (C7) cross-check; the 71-dataset CC18 sweep behind C1/C3 (~3-4 h) is explicitly out of scope for this budget.

repo/README.md: 162 lines
    1| # Ternary Decision Trees with Locally-Adaptive Uncertainty Zones
    2| 
    3| [![Python 3.9+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.9+-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/)
    4| [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE)
    5| 
    6| ## Paper
    7| 
    8| This repository accompanies the paper:
    9| 
   10| **Ternary Decision Trees with Locally-Adaptive Uncertainty Zones**
   11| William Smits — *Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery (under review)*
   12| arXiv: [XXXX.XXXXX](https://arxiv.org/abs/XXXX.XXXXX)
   13| 
   14| > Standard decision trees make hard binary routing decisions at each node,
   15| > assigning identical confidence to instances far from a decision boundary
   16| > and to those directly on it. We introduce ternary decision trees, which
   17| > augment each split node with a locally-computed uncertainty zone.
   18| > Instances whose feature value falls within this zone receive predictions
   19| > formed by weighted blending of both child subtrees and are flagged as
   20| > boundary-uncertain. Five methods for computing the zone half-width δ
   21| > are proposed and evaluated across 72 OpenML-CC18 datasets, three
   22| > Breiman synthetic benchmarks with known Bayes errors, and four
   23| > medical and financial datasets.
   24| 
   25| ---
   26| 
   27| ## Installation
   28| 
   29| ```bash
   30| # Using uv (recommended)
   31| uv pip install -e .
   32| 
   33| # Using pip
   34| pip install -e .
   35| ```
   36| 
   37| Requires Python ≥ 3.9.
   38| 
   39| ---
   40| 
   41| ## Quick Start
   42| 
   43| ```python
   44| from ternary_tree import BinaryTernaryTree, TrinaryTree, make_classifier
   45| from sklearn.datasets import load_breast_cancer
   46| from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
   47| 
   48| X, y = load_breast_cancer(return_X_y=True)
   49| X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, random_state=42)
   50| 
   51| # Recommended: margin delta method with probabilistic routing
   52| clf = make_classifier(delta_method="margin", routing_method="probabilistic")
   53| clf.fit(X_train, y_train)
   54| 
   55| pred    = clf.predict(X_test)           # class predictions
   56| ternary = clf.predict_ternary(X_test)   # 1=decided, 0=boundary-uncertain
   57| proba   = clf.predict_proba(X_test)     # probability distributions
   58| ```
   59| 
   60| ---
   61| 
   62| ## Five Delta Methods
   63| 
   64| | Method | Description | Hyperparameters |
   65| |---|---|---|
   66| | `margin` | Distance to nearest cross-class training example (recommended) | None |

    2| delta_methods.py
    3| ================
    4| Four methods for computing the node-local Undecided-zone half-width δ.
    5| 
    6| Each method takes the data available at the current node after the best
    7| split has been found, and returns a non-negative float δ.
    8| 
    9| The four methods
   10| ----------------
   11| 1. quality_plateau
   12|    Reads the plateau of the split quality curve. δ = half the width of the
   13|    region where Q(θ) ≥ (1 - ε) × Q(θ*).  Zero extra computation — the
   14|    quality curve is already evaluated by find_best_split.
   15| 
   16| 2. class_overlap
   17|    Empirical class-distribution overlap. δ = half the width of the feature
   18|    range where both (or all) class percentile bands intersect.
   19| 
   20| 3. gain_ratio
   21|    δ = α × feature_range / (1 + GR) where GR = IG / H_split.
   22|    High gain ratio → confident split → small δ.
   23|    Low gain ratio  → uncertain split → large δ.
   24| 
   25| 4. node_bootstrap
   26|    Bootstrap the node data B times, find the optimal threshold each time,
   27|    set δ = std(optimal_thresholds).  Most statistically principled;
   28|    most expensive (but still fast for small node sizes).
   29| 
   30| All methods clamp δ to [0, max_fraction × feature_range] to prevent
   31| degenerate cases where δ would encompass the whole feature range.

  252| # Method 5: Margin-Based (SVM-inspired)
  253| # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  254| 
  255| def delta_margin(
  256|     col    : np.ndarray,
  257|     y      : np.ndarray,
  258|     theta  : float,
  259|     classes: np.ndarray,
  260| ) -> float:
  261|     """δ = distance from θ* to the nearest cross-class example on either side.
  262| 
  263|     Directly analogous to the SVM margin.  After the optimal threshold θ* has
  264|     been chosen, examine which training examples of each class sit closest to
  265|     the boundary but on the "wrong" side — i.e. the examples that most challenge
  266|     the chosen split.
  267| 
  268|     Algorithm
  269|     ---------
  270|     1. Identify the dominant class on each side of θ* (left_class, right_class).
  271|     2. Find cross-class intrusions:
  272|          right_intrusions: left_class examples that appear to the RIGHT of θ*
  273|          left_intrusions : right_class examples that appear to the LEFT of θ*
  274|     3. δ = distance from θ* to the nearest intrusion on either side.
  275|     4. If the split is perfectly clean (no intrusions), fall back to the
  276|        physical gap: (nearest_right - nearest_left) / 2.
  277|        A large physical gap means few examples constrain the boundary —
  278|        the boundary could reasonably be placed anywhere in that gap.
  279| 
  280|     No hyperparameters.  The margin is read directly from the data.
  281| 
  282|     Parameters
  283|     ----------
  284|     col     : feature column at this node (unsorted)
  285|     y       : class labels at this node
  286|     theta   : the chosen optimal split threshold θ*
  287|     classes : sorted unique class labels
  288|     """
  289|     left_mask  = col <= theta
  290|     right_mask = ~left_mask
  291| 
  292|     n_left  = int(left_mask.sum())
  293|     n_right = int(right_mask.sum())
  294| 
  295|     if n_left == 0 or n_right == 0:
  296|         return 0.0
  297| 
  298|     # Dominant class on each side (by count)
  299|     y_left  = y[left_mask]
  300|     y_right = y[right_mask]
  301| 
  302|     unique_left,  counts_left  = np.unique(y_left,  return_counts=True)
  303|     unique_right, counts_right = np.unique(y_right, return_counts=True)
  304| 
  305|     left_dominant  = unique_left[np.argmax(counts_left)]
  306|     right_dominant = unique_right[np.argmax(counts_right)]
  307| 
  308|     if left_dominant == right_dominant:
  309|         # Same class dominates both sides — split is not informative.
  310|         # Fall back to physical gap / 2.
  311|         left_gap  = theta - float(col[left_mask].max())
  312|         right_gap = float(col[right_mask].min()) - theta
  313|         return _clamp_delta(min(left_gap, right_gap), col)

    1| """
    2| binary_ternary_tree.py
    3| ======================
    4| BinaryTernaryTree: a CART-style decision tree whose PREDICTION phase is
    5| ternary.
    6| 
    7| Training phase
    8| --------------
    9| Identical to standard CART — examples route left if x ≤ θ, right if x > θ.
   10| During fitting, δ is computed at each node using the chosen delta method and
   11| stored in the SplitNode.  δ does not affect which child receives which
   12| training examples.
   13| 
   14| Prediction phase
   15| ----------------
   16| At each node, an example is routed based on both θ and δ:
   17| 
   18|   x ≤ θ - δ  →  clear False  →  go left (standard routing)
   19|   x > θ + δ  →  clear True   →  go right (standard routing)
   20|   θ-δ < x ≤ θ+δ  →  Undecided zone  →  routing_method determines behaviour
   21| 
   22| Two routing methods:
   23| 
   24|   'probabilistic'
   25|       Recurse into BOTH children with distance-based weights:
   26|           w_left  = (θ + δ - x) / (2δ)
   27|           w_right = (x - (θ - δ)) / (2δ)
   28|       Each child's probability vector is weighted and summed.
   29|       Uncertainty compounds down the tree — a sample that is undecided at
   30|       multiple nodes gets progressively smeared across leaves.
   31| 
   32|   'deferred'
   33|       Get predictions from left and right children using HARD binary routing
   34|       (no further ternary routing), then combine:
   35|           proba = w_left × hard_left_proba + w_right × hard_right_proba
   36|       Uncertainty is resolved in one step — subsequent nodes use crisp
   37|       thresholds regardless of further undecided zones.
   38| 
   39| Ternary output
   40| --------------
   41| predict_ternary(X) returns int8 array:
   42|   1  = DECIDED  — sample traversed no undecided zone
   43|   0  = UNDECIDED — sample entered at least one undecided zone
   44|

    3| ==========
    4| Ternary-specific evaluation metrics.
    5| 
    6| Standard metrics (accuracy, f1) treat all predictions equally.

    8| allowing measurement of the accuracy-vs-coverage tradeoff.

   12| decided_rate(ternary_verdict)

   16|     Fraction of instances that received an UNDECIDED verdict (0).
   17| 
   18| decided_accuracy(y_true, y_pred, ternary_verdict)
   19|     Accuracy computed ONLY on instances the classifier decided on.
   20|     The core quality metric for ternary classifiers:
   21|     high decided_accuracy + meaningful undecided_rate = good system.
   22| 
   23| decided_f1(y_true, y_pred, ternary_verdict, average)
   24|     F1 score on decided instances only.
   25| 
   26| ternary_summary(y_true, y_pred, ternary_verdict)

    1| """
    2| splitter.py
    3| ===========
    4| Core split evaluation engine.
    5| 
    6| Provides O(n log n) evaluation of Gini gain and Information Gain across all
    7| candidate thresholds for one feature using cumulative weighted class counts.
    8| This is the standard CART histogram trick.  All four delta methods and both
    9| tree classes use these functions — they are the single source of truth for
   10| split quality.
   11| 
   12| Key functions
   13| -------------
   14| evaluate_all_thresholds(col, y, sample_weight, criterion)
   15|     Returns (candidates, scores, parent_impurity, split_info) for one feature.
   16| 
   17| find_best_split(X, y, sample_weight, criterion, feature_indices)
   18|     Searches across features; returns best (feature_idx, threshold, score,
   19|     candidates_for_best_feature, scores_for_best_feature, split_info).
   20| 
   21| compute_class_probabilities(y, sample_weight, classes)
   22|     Weighted class probability vector for a leaf node.
   23| """
   24| 
   25| from __future__ import annotations
   26| 
   27| import numpy as np
   28| from typing import List, Optional, Tuple
   29| 
   30| 
   31| # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   32| # Impurity helpers
   33| # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   34| 
   35| def _gini(probs: np.ndarray) -> float:
   36|     return 1.0 - float(np.sum(probs ** 2))
   37| 
   38| 
   39| def _entropy(probs: np.ndarray) -> float:
   40|     p = probs[probs > 0]
   41|     return float(-np.sum(p * np.log2(p)))
   42| 
   43| 
   44| def _split_entropy(left_w: float, right_w: float, total_w: float) -> float:
   45|     """Binary entropy of the split proportions (used for gain ratio)."""
   46|     result = 0.0
   47|     for w in (left_w, right_w):
   48|         p = w / total_w
   49|         if p > 0:
   50|             result -= p * np.log2(p)
   51|     return result
   52|

"""Download the OpenML datasets used by the reproduction and cache them.

Reusable raw artifacts are stored under $REPRO_DATA_CACHE/openml (shared across
runs) so a clean re-run does not re-download.  Only credit-g (the pinned target
C2) is fetched by default; extra datasets are opt-in via argv.
"""
import os
import sys
import json
import numpy as np

CACHE = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE") or os.path.join(".", ".cache")
OPENML_CACHE = os.path.join(CACHE, "ternary_tree_openml")
os.makedirs(OPENML_CACHE, exist_ok=True)

# name -> OpenML dataset id (see benchmark/datasets_extended.py in the repo)
IDS = {
    "credit-g": 31,
    "diabetes": 37,
    "heart-c": 53,
    "mammography": 310,
    "twonorm": 1507,
}


def main():
    import openml
    openml.config.cache_directory = OPENML_CACHE

    names = sys.argv[1:] or ["credit-g"]
    out = {}
    for name in names:
        did = IDS[name]
        print(f"fetching {name} (openml id {did}) ...", flush=True)
        ds = openml.datasets.get_dataset(did, download_data=True, cache=True)
        X, y, attr_names, class_vals = ds.get_data(
            target=ds.default_target_attribute, dataset_format="dataframe"
        )
        print(f"  ok: shape={X.shape} target={ds.default_target_attribute} "
              f"classes={list(class_vals) if class_vals is not None else '?'}")
        out[name] = {
            "dataset_id": did,
            "openml_name": ds.name,
            "n_rows": int(X.shape[0]),
            "n_cols": int(X.shape[1]),
            "target": ds.default_target_attribute,
            "attributes": [str(a) for a in X.columns],
            "dtypes": {str(a): str(t) for a, t in X.dtypes.items()},
            "class_values": [str(c) for c in (class_vals or [])],
            "target_counts": {str(k): int(v) for k, v in y.value_counts().items()},
        }
        # persist a plain CSV copy next to the openml cache for robustness
        ds_path = os.path.join(OPENML_CACHE, f"{name}.csv")
        Xa = X.copy()
        Xa[ds.default_target_attribute or "target"] = y
        Xa.to_csv(ds_path, index=False)
        print(f"  wrote {ds_path} ({os.path.getsize(ds_path)} bytes)")

    with open(os.path.join(OPENML_CACHE, "dataset_info.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(out, f, indent=2)
    print(json.dumps(out, indent=2)[:3000])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Probe: run the authors' loader + margin/probabilistic tree on credit-g."""
import os, sys, time
import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("repo"))
CACHE = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE") or ".cache"
import openml
openml.config.cache_directory = os.path.join(CACHE, "openml_dl")

from benchmark.datasets_extended import _preprocess  # noqa: E402
from ternary_tree import make_classifier            # noqa: E402
from ternary_tree.metrics import ternary_summary    # noqa: E402
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold # noqa: E402
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler    # noqa: E402
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier     # noqa: E402

ds = openml.datasets.get_dataset(31, download_data=True)
Xr, yr, _, _ = ds.get_data(target=ds.default_target_attribute, dataset_format="array")
X, y = _preprocess(Xr, yr)
print("X", X.shape, X.dtype, "y", y.shape, np.bincount(y), "nan", np.isnan(X).sum())

SEED, CV, DEPTH = 42, 5, 4
skf = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=CV, shuffle=True, random_state=SEED)
rows = []
for fi, (tr, te) in enumerate(skf.split(X, y)):
    sc = StandardScaler()
    Xtr, Xte = sc.fit_transform(X[tr]), sc.transform(X[te])
    ytr, yte = y[tr], y[te]
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    clf = make_classifier(delta_method="margin", routing_method="probabilistic",
                          max_depth=DEPTH, random_state=SEED)
    clf.fit(Xtr, ytr)
    pred = clf.predict(Xte)
    ver = clf.predict_ternary(Xte)
    m = ternary_summary(yte, pred, ver)
    base = DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=DEPTH, random_state=SEED).fit(Xtr, ytr)
    bacc = float((base.predict(Xte) == yte).mean())
    rows.append((m, bacc))
    print(f"fold {fi}: dec_acc={m['decided_accuracy']:.4f} undec={m['undecided_rate']:.3f} "
          f"acc_all={m['accuracy_all']:.4f} f1dec={m['decided_f1']:.3f} cart={bacc:.4f} "
          f"t={time.perf_counter()-t0:.2f}s")

dec = np.mean([r[0]["decided_accuracy"] for r in rows])
und = np.mean([r[0]["undecided_rate"] for r in rows])
aca = np.mean([r[0]["accuracy_all"] for r in rows])
f1d = np.mean([r[0]["decided_f1"] for r in rows])
cart = np.mean([r[1] for r in rows])
print(f"MEAN dec_acc={dec:.4f} undec={und:.4f} acc_all={aca:.4f} f1dec={f1d:.3f} cart={cart:.4f}")
print("target: dec 0.6808 undec 0.481 acc_all 0.7130 f1dec 0.584 cart 0.7130")

"""
metrics.py
==========
Ternary-specific evaluation metrics.

Standard metrics (accuracy, f1) treat all predictions equally.
Ternary metrics separate DECIDED instances from UNDECIDED instances,
allowing measurement of the accuracy-vs-coverage tradeoff.

Key metrics
-----------
decided_rate(ternary_verdict)
    Fraction of instances that received a DECIDED verdict (1).

undecided_rate(ternary_verdict)
    Fraction of instances that received an UNDECIDED verdict (0).

decided_accuracy(y_true, y_pred, ternary_verdict)
    Accuracy computed ONLY on instances the classifier decided on.
    The core quality metric for ternary classifiers:
    high decided_accuracy + meaningful undecided_rate = good system.

decided_f1(y_true, y_pred, ternary_verdict, average)
    F1 score on decided instances only.

ternary_summary(y_true, y_pred, ternary_verdict)
    Returns a dict with all metrics in one call.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict

import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score, f1_score


def decided_rate(ternary_verdict: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Fraction of instances with DECIDED verdict (1)."""
    return float(np.mean(ternary_verdict == 1))


def undecided_rate(ternary_verdict: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Fraction of instances with UNDECIDED verdict (0)."""
    return float(np.mean(ternary_verdict == 0))


def decided_accuracy(
    y_true         : np.ndarray,
    y_pred         : np.ndarray,
    ternary_verdict: np.ndarray,
) -> float:
    """Accuracy on instances where classifier issued a DECIDED verdict.

    Returns NaN if no instances are decided.
    """
    mask = ternary_verdict == 1
    if mask.sum() == 0:
        return float("nan")
    return float(accuracy_score(y_true[mask], y_pred[mask]))


def decided_f1(
    y_true         : np.ndarray,
    y_pred         : np.ndarray,
    ternary_verdict: np.ndarray,
    average        : str = "macro",
) -> float:
    """F1 score on instances where classifier issued a DECIDED verdict."""
    mask = ternary_verdict == 1
    if mask.sum() == 0:
        return float("nan")
    return float(f1_score(y_true[mask], y_pred[mask], average=average, zero_division=0))


def overall_accuracy(y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """Standard accuracy on all instances (undecided included)."""
    return float(accuracy_score(y_true, y_pred))


def ternary_summary(
    y_true         : np.ndarray,
    y_pred         : np.ndarray,
    ternary_verdict: np.ndarray,
    average        : str = "macro",
) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """All ternary metrics in one dict."""
    return {
        "accuracy_all"     : overall_accuracy(y_true, y_pred),
        "decided_rate"     : decided_rate(ternary_verdict),

Four methods for computing the node-local Undecided-zone half-width δ.

Each method takes the data available at the current node after the best

2. class_overlap
   Empirical class-distribution overlap. δ = half the width of the feature

def delta_margin(
    col    : np.ndarray,
    y      : np.ndarray,
    theta  : float,
    classes: np.ndarray,
) -> float:
    """δ = distance from θ* to the nearest cross-class example on either side.

    Directly analogous to the SVM margin.  After the optimal threshold θ* has
    been chosen, examine which training examples of each class sit closest to
    the boundary but on the "wrong" side — i.e. the examples that most challenge
    the chosen split.

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Reproduction of C2 from "Ternary Decision Trees with Locally-Adaptive
Uncertainty Zones" (arXiv 2605.22740).

Target (C2, Table 4 / Table 5 / Table 8, credit-g row, Margin + probabilistic
routing, 5-fold stratified CV, max_depth=4):
    decided accuracy ~0.6808, boundary-uncertain rate ~0.481,
    overall accuracy ~0.7130, F1-decided ~0.584, CART baseline ~0.7130.

Everything is computed from data by this script; nothing is hard-coded.

The implementation is the authors' released library, used unmodified from
./repo (ternary_tree.make_classifier -> BinaryTernaryTree with the Eq.-10
margin delta in ternary_tree/delta_methods.py and probabilistic blending in
ternary_tree/binary_ternary_tree.py).  The evaluation protocol mirrors the
authors' own runner benchmark/run_extended_benchmark.py:
StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42), StandardScaler
fitted on the training part of each fold only, max_depth=4, and the same
sklearn DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=4) baseline on identical folds.

Usage
-----
python reproduce.py                # full target run (credit-g, 5 folds)
python reproduce.py --smoke        # 1 fold, 200-row subsample sanity check
python reproduce.py --secondary    # + diabetes / mammography / twonorm checks
python reproduce.py --sensitivity  # + unshuffled-fold sensitivity check

OPENML_ROOT = os.path.join(CACHE, "openml_root")
CSV_CACHE = os.path.join(CACHE, "ternary_tree_openml")
LOCAL_DATA = os.path.join(HERE, "data")
RESULTS = os.path.join(HERE, "results")

SEED = 42            # paper Appendix E
N_SPLITS = 5         # paper Sec. 5.2
MAX_DEPTH = 4        # paper Sec. 5.2

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Imports from the authors' code (no repo file is modified)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
from benchmark.datasets_extended import _preprocess          # noqa: E402
from ternary_tree import make_classifier                      # noqa: E402
from ternary_tree.metrics import ternary_summary              # noqa: E402
from ternary_tree.node import LeafNode, SplitNode             # noqa: E402

from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold           # noqa: E402
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler              # noqa: E402
from sklearn.tree import DecisionTreeClassifier               # noqa: E402

# OpenML dataset ids used by the authors' loaders (benchmark/datasets_extended.py)

    "credit-g": 31,        # C2 target, also in the CC18 suite (task 31)
    "diabetes": 37,        # C7
    "heart-c": 53,
    "mammography": 310,    # C5
    "twonorm": 1507,       # C6
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def load_dataset(name: str, verbose: bool = True):
    """Load an OpenML dataset by name through the authors' preprocessing path.

    Tries, in order: the shared REPRO_DATA_CACHE openml root, a cached CSV copy,
    a workspace-local CSV copy, then a fresh download.  Returns (X, y, info).
    """
    did = DATASET_IDS[name]
    X = y = None
    source = None

    # 1) openml package (its own cache lives in the shared REPRO_DATA_CACHE)
    try:
        import openml
        try:
            openml.config.set_root_cache_directory(OPENML_ROOT)
        except Exception:
            pass
        ds = openml.datasets.get_dataset(did, download_data=True)
        Xr, yr, _, _ = ds.get_data(
            target=ds.default_target_attribute, dataset_format="array"
        )
        source = f"openml:dataset:{did}"
        # keep a plain CSV copy in the shared cache for offline re-runs
        try:
            os.makedirs(CSV_CACHE, exist_ok=True)
            import pandas as pd
            df = pd.DataFrame(Xr)
            df[ds.default_target_attribute] = yr
            df.to_csv(os.path.join(CSV_CACHE, f"{name}_raw.csv"), index=False)
        except Exception:
            pass
    except Exception as e:  # network / server problems -> CSV fallbacks
        if verbose:
            print(f"  [openml failed for {name}: {e}; trying cached CSV]")

    if X is None:
        import pandas as pd
        for p in (os.path.join(CSV_CACHE, f"{name}_raw.csv"),
                  os.path.join(LOCAL_DATA, f"{name}_raw.csv")):
            if os.path.exists(p):
                df = pd.read_csv(p)
                tgt = df.columns[-1]
                Xr = df.drop(columns=[tgt]).to_numpy(dtype=object)
                yr = df[tgt].to_numpy()
                source = f"csv:{p}"
                break

    if X is None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"could not obtain dataset {name} (id {did})")

    X, y = _preprocess(Xr, yr)
    info = {
        "name": name,
        "dataset_id": did,
        "n_samples": int(X.shape[0]),
        "n_features": int(X.shape[1]),
        "n_classes": int(len(np.unique(y))),
        "class_counts": {str(k): int(v) for k, v in zip(*np.unique(y, return_counts=True))},
        "source": source,
    }
    if verbose:
        print(f"  loaded {name}: N={info['n_samples']} d={info['n_features']} "
              f"classes={info['class_counts']} [{source}]")
    return X, y, info

def single_split(X, y, delta_method, routing_method, seed=SEED, max_depth=MAX_DEPTH,
                 train_size=200, verbose=True, tag="smoke"):
    """Smoke path: one stratified train/test pass through the same code path."""
    tr, te = train_test_split(np.arange(len(y)), train_size=train_size,
                              stratify=y, random_state=seed)
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    X_tr, X_te = scaler.fit_transform(X[tr]), scaler.transform(X[te])
    y_tr, y_te = y[tr], y[te]

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        clf = make_classifier(delta_method=delta_method, routing_method=routing_method,
                              random_state=seed, **_tree_config(int(len(y_tr)), max_depth))
        clf.fit(X_tr, y_tr)
        pred = clf.predict(X_te)
        verdict = clf.predict_ternary(X_te)

    m = ternary_summary(y_te, pred, verdict)
    assert set(np.unique(verdict)) <= {0, 1}, "verdict must be binary 0/1"
    assert np.allclose(clf.predict_proba(X_te).sum(axis=1), 1.0), \
        "blended probability rows must sum to 1"

    base = DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=max_depth, random_state=seed)
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        base.fit(X_tr, y_tr)
        cart_acc = float((base.predict(X_te) == y_te).mean())

    diag = delta_diagnostics(clf.tree_, np.ptp(X_tr, axis=0))
    out = {
        "dataset": tag, "n_train": int(len(tr)), "n_test": int(len(te)),
        "split": f"single stratified split (train_size={train_size}, random_state={seed})",
        "fit_metrics": m,
        "cart_baseline_accuracy": cart_acc,
        "split_nodes": diag["n_nodes"],
        "nodes_delta_pos": diag["n_pos"],
        "nodes_delta_clamped": diag["n_clamped"],
        "mean_delta_over_range": (diag["sum_rel"] / diag["n_nodes"]
                                  if diag["n_nodes"] else 0.0),
        "max_delta_over_range": float(max(diag["rel"])) if diag["rel"] else 0.0,
    }
    if verbose:
        print(f"    smoke: dec_acc={m['decided_accuracy']:.4f} "
              f"undec={m['undecided_rate']:.3f} acc_all={m['accuracy_all']:.4f} "
              f"cart={cart_acc:.4f}  nodes d>0 {diag['n_pos']}/{diag['n_nodes']} "
              f"(clamped {diag['n_clamped']}, max d/range {out['max_delta_over_range']:.3f})")
    return out
